title: Unhandled promise rejections and process.on
hook: A rejected promise with no .catch handler becomes an unhandled rejection — not the same as a synchronous throw. Node.js can exit; browsers log to the console. You must attach handlers at process and promise boundaries.

blocks.text: When a **Promise** rejects and nothing handles that rejection — no `.catch()`, no `await` inside `try/catch`, no `.then(_, onRejected)` — the runtime emits an **unhandledrejection** event (browser) or **unhandledRejection** on `process` (Node.js). This is separate from a synchronous **throw**: `try/catch` around code that *returns* a rejected promise without `await` will not catch it. Unhandled rejections are the async equivalent of an uncaught exception and often indicate a missing `.catch` at a boundary.

entries.plainDefinition: A Promise settled with a failure reason via reject() or throw inside an async executor.
Browser event when a promise rejects with no handler attached by the time the microtask queue drains.
Node.js process event for the same situation. Default behavior may exit the process with a non-zero code.
A throw that never hits catch — different channel from unhandled rejection but both need top-level handlers in servers.

blocks.text: Server processes that leave rejections unhandled can exit mid-request, corrupt in-flight work, or succeed HTTP responses while background tasks fail silently. C# has a parallel story with **unobserved Task exceptions** — module 13 covers async deeply; here the rule is simple: every promise chain needs a terminal handler at the worker boundary, and Node services register `process.on('unhandledRejection')` for last-resort logging.

blocks.title: try/catch does not catch bare promises
blocks.body: try { doAsync(); } catch — useless if doAsync returns a promise. You need try { await doAsync(); } catch or doAsync().catch(...).

blocks.title: From reject to crash or log

items.title: Promise rejects
items.body: async function throw, Promise.reject, or failed await inside async propagates a rejection.

items.title: Microtask schedules handlers
items.body: Attached .catch or awaiting parent gets a chance to run in the same tick or soon after.

items.title: No handler found
items.body: Runtime emits unhandledrejection / unhandledRejection with the reason (often an Error).

items.title: Host policy
items.body: Browser: console error (may not kill the tab). Node 15+: default may terminate. Always handle at boundaries in production servers.

diagram.title: Sync throw vs unhandled rejection
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  SYNC[throw in sync code] --> TC{try/catch?}
  TC -->|yes| HANDLED[Handled]
  TC -->|no| UNCAUGHT[uncaughtException]
  ASYNC[Promise rejects] --> AW{await or .catch?}
  AW -->|yes| HANDLED2[Handled]
  AW -->|no| UNH[unhandledRejection]
  UNH --> NODE[Node may exit]
  UNCAUGHT --> NODE2[Node may exit]

snippet.label: try/catch only works with await
snippet.explanation: Line 8: calling async function without await returns a pending promise — try/catch sees no throw. Line 17: await transfers rejection into catch as a synchronous-looking flow.

snippet.label: Node.js process-level handlers
snippet.explanation: Line 1: last-resort net for stray promises. Line 6: sync throws that escape. Line 12: per-request try/catch still required — process handlers are not a substitute for boundary handling.

snippet.label: Browser unhandledrejection
snippet.explanation: Line 1: global listener for debugging. Line 9: fire-and-forget fetch without .catch is a classic unhandled rejection source.

snippet.label: Failure mode: forEach with async callbacks
snippet.explanation: Line 5: forEach ignores returned promises — async throws become unhandled. Line 12: Promise.all surfaces the first rejection to an outer await/catch.

blocks.title: Async failure channels
rows: Node may exit on unhandled rejection
Host logs; process may continue or stop

blocks.title: Relying only on process.on
blocks.body: Global handlers are for logging and graceful shutdown — not normal control flow. Every route, job, and event listener should catch and forward errors.

blocks.title: Swallowing in unhandledRejection
blocks.body: Calling event.preventDefault() or returning without fixing the missing .catch hides symptoms. Fix the promise chain, then optionally suppress duplicate console noise.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: APM tools and Node --unhandled-rejections=strict catch missing handlers in CI. rejectionHandled event fires if a late .catch attaches — rare race in dynamic code. Promise.all vs allSettled: all rejects fast on first failure; allSettled never rejects — choose based on whether partial success is valid. In worker threads, unhandled rejections in the worker emit error on the parent Worker object. Domains (deprecated) and AsyncLocalStorage help correlate request context in logs. C# Task unobserved exceptions surface on finalizer thread unless TaskScheduler hooks observe them — different timing, same class of bug: fire-and-forget async.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying try/catch around async() without await catches rejections. Not knowing Node exit policy on unhandledRejection. Using forEach with async without Promise.all. Confusing unhandled rejection with uncaughtException.

interviewTakeaways: Rejected promises need await in try or .catch — sync try/catch alone is not enough.
Node: process.on('unhandledRejection') and uncaughtException for last-resort handling.
60s: Async errors are promises. await in try. Boundary .catch. Never forEach async without Promise.all.
Follow-up: what is the difference between unhandledRejection and uncaughtException in Node?
commonPitfalls: try { asyncFn(); } catch — never catches rejection.
forEach with async callback — unhandled rejections.
Strong answer: 'await in try. Terminal catch at boundary. process.on for logging only. Promise.all to aggregate async work.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# Tasks that fault without await or .ContinueWith can raise UnobservedTaskException. JavaScript unhandledRejection is the direct parallel.
TypeScript does not track unhandled rejections. Explicit void or .catch documents fire-and-forget intent.
